summary:
Macro Hive interview (c. mid-2023) with Graham founder Ken Tropin on running a macro fund: career, macro as diversifier, why 2010-2021 was quiet and 2022 rich in central-bank action (30x more hikes), and his market views (short equities, weak dollar, steepener).
Core ideas: macro/CTA is uncorrelated alpha whose opportunity set follows central bank activity and volatility; diversify alpha sources; daily risk meeting.

coverage.note: intro; Tropin career and Graham history; discretionary business 1998
macro in crises 1987/2000/2008; quiet 2010-2021 central banks
central bank move counts; outlook for inflation; macro share of AUM
allocation outlook; investor portfolio risk; macro fund edge
risk meeting; alpha diversification; pod shops
curve, duration risk, cuts, crisis risk, US outlook

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: in 1998 in an effort to diversify the sources of alpha that Graham is able to take advantage of we began to build a discretionary business
claims.claim: Graham began as a systematic CTA (1994) and added a discretionary macro business in 1998 to diversify alpha sources; a fed-watcher trader was the catalyst for its success.
claims.testable: no: firm history relevant to diversification

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: the markets are pretty inefficient back then so it was uh you know not unreasonable to uh try and generate really high rates of return
claims.claim: Early CTAs/macro earned high returns because markets were less efficient and an immature industry offered edge.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: you could have a source of alpha totally uncorrelated to STS and bonds
claims.claim: Macro traders' appeal was returns uncorrelated to stocks and bonds, unlike other investments.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: macro is really about trading in four asset classes either directionally or from a Rel value point of view
claims.claim: Tropin's definition: macro trades equities, FX, fixed income and commodities, directionally or relative value, over short or long horizons, typically directional in orientation.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: it wasn't meant to be layering on more beta risk it was meant to be diversifying from beta risk
claims.claim: Hedge funds were intended to diversify from market beta; macro was dominant in the first decade of the industry for that reason.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: our CTA got long fixed income and made a and made a lot of money so it was an excellent diversifying
claims.claim: Crisis episodes where CTAs/macro diversified: 1987 crash (short equities, long bonds after the Monday), 2000-2003 equity bear, second half of 2008.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: every Central Bank was easing um and was more or less uh not only easing but giving forward guidance
claims.claim: 2010-2021 was quiet for macro because central banks eased and gave forward guidance that removed rate uncertainty and volatility.
claims.testable: yes: compare macro returns vs policy move counts

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: there were a total a total of 1325 basis point rate hike equivalent moves in 11 years by three
claims.claim: July 2010 to July 2021 the ECB, Fed and BoE made about 1325bp of hike-equivalent moves in total (about 1.2 hikes per year), versus just under 50 25bp-equivalent hikes in 2022 alone: 30x the action.
claims.indicator: count of central bank rate changes (ECB, Fed, BoE)

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: the opportunity set is is so much more constructive um in an environment where central banks are are are moving a lot and there's heightened volatility in FX
claims.claim: Macro opportunity set depends on central bank activity and volatility in FX, rates, equities and commodities; high-activity regimes are favourable.
claims.direction: long macro/CTA allocation when central banks move a lot

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: inflation is kind of like an ocean liner it's hard to move around it was really hard for them to create it
claims.claim: Tropin's view (2023): inflation is slow to return to 2% as fast as markets expect, so heightened volatility persists for 36-60 months, with supply chains, Ukraine, Asia tension, US election and green-energy policy as reasons.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: macro was probably half of the industry maybe even the highest 70% of the industry in the 90s and and now it's more like 15 or 20%
claims.claim: Macro's share of hedge fund AUM fell from about 50-70% in the 1990s to about 15-20% now.
claims.indicator: macro share of hedge fund AUM

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: if their macro allocation is 10% of their portfolio maybe it'll go to 15 I don't know
claims.claim: Expectation that investors lift macro allocations (e.g. 10% to 15%) as the opportunity set improves.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I'm kind of um uncomfortable uh if I'm a traditional investor uh today looking ahead of a stock and bond portfolio
claims.claim: Traditional stock/bond portfolios look risky: inflation not priced, duration risk with no term premium on an inverted curve, expensive equities. SVB failed from unpriced duration; macro funds diversify as uncorrelated.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I think experience is is really a big deal right the fact that you know we've been doing this for 29 years
claims.claim: Edge in a macro fund: experience across cycles and events, steady conservative management, talent, culture and risk management.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: we started having a daily risk meeting at 9:30 every morning to look at um every Traders positions liquidity
claims.claim: Graham has held a daily 9:30 risk meeting since 2007 reviewing P&L, positions, liquidity, counterparty risk and stress tests; hands-on risk management adds value over the long haul.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I don't want to only make money when it's good for momentum and quantitative trading I want to be able to make uh a return uh when uh you know maybe value is a more attractive Factor than momentum
claims.claim: Diversify internal alpha sources (systematic momentum, discretionary macro, long-term quant equities) so returns are not reliant on momentum alone.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: there's no way you can do what worked 10 years ago and expect it to always work in the future
claims.claim: Strategies need continual innovation, as what worked 10 years ago will not always work.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: some of them are uncomfortable with the pass through fee structure uh because the costs end up getting pretty high
claims.claim: Pod-shop multi-manager structures have pass-through fees and long lockups that some clients dislike; Graham launched its own macro-focused multi-strategy fund to compete for talent.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I don't want to predict that uh it's going to replace humans uh in terms of strategic judgment and uh I think there's an edge that humans have that is hard to replicate
claims.claim: AI is powerful, but Tropin sees human strategic judgment as an edge not yet replaceable.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: with forward pees onee PE now just under 19 that seems high to me uh should we normalize at 16 or 17 I would think so
claims.claim: Tropin (2023) saw equities expensive: forward P/E near 19 versus normal 16-17, a likely recession with tech layoffs shrinking earnings, so leaned short equities.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: what drove equities higher it really is the Tina phenomenon there is no alternative and now there is an alternative now you can make four or five% in RIS stre
claims.claim: With 4-5% risk-free rates, TINA no longer supports equities, a headwind for stocks.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: the psychology of investor for the last 15 years is buy every dip and you were rewarded for doing so
claims.claim: Buy-the-dip psychology kept equities rising despite his bearish thesis; his reason investors still buy is the Fed being near done.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: the perception is the ECB is now more hawkish than the Fed and uh so you know the
claims.claim: The dollar looked slightly weak to Tropin (EUR/USD trying to break above 1.10) as the ECB was seen more hawkish than the Fed after a 15-month strong dollar.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I think the yield curve should steepen more it's it's already steepened some it was as you know it was inverted as much as two1 were 100 basis points inverted now it's about 60
claims.claim: The 2s10s curve had been 100bp inverted and was about 60bp; he expected further steepening as the economy enters recession.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: people totally forgot about something called duration risk uh and that you should get paid more you should have term premium for taking duration risk
claims.claim: Duration risk was unpriced (no term premium), as SVB showed; the steepener is the more interesting rates trade than direction.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I think the Market's slightly optimistic on Cuts particularly in the US happening in this third and fourth quarter
claims.claim: Markets priced 30-40bp of Fed cuts in late 2023; Tropin was not convinced the Fed could cut, a modest mispricing.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I don't think we'll see an' 08 style crisis uh although we came pretty close two weeks ago right I mean uh you know uh the run on Banks
claims.claim: No 2008-style crisis expected: the Fed response to the bank runs was good, but risks (debt ceiling, Ukraine, politics) call for vigilance.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: attitude is important show up first leave last never be on the computer computer screwing around
claims.claim: Career advice for young macro traders: find mentors and inspiring colleagues, show up first and leave last, keep a positive attitude, and recruit talent where others do not look.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: we have a hybrid Approach at gram of uh you know three and two
claims.claim: Graham uses a hybrid 3-days-in-office, 2-days-remote policy; he prefers collaboration in person.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: I don't know that the markets are going to be as um amazingly good for macro as they were in 22 in the next two three years
claims.claim: Tropin expects macro to be less spectacular than 2022 but more interesting than 2010-2021 in the next 2-3 years, remaining non-correlated to other investments.

claims.speaker: Ken Tropin
claims.quote: you got to read reminiscence of a stock operator lefur and uh you've got to read Jack schwager uh you know Market Wizards
claims.claim: Recommended reading: Reminiscences of a Stock Operator and Market Wizards.
